prompt: Test whether a single bit of an int is 1: build a mask with 1 << bit and check it against the value with &.
explanation: 1 << bit produces a mask with exactly one 1 in the position being tested; ANDing it with the value zeroes every other bit, so the result is nonzero exactly when the tested bit was set. Comparing with != 0 rather than == mask matters for bit 31: 1 << 31 is Integer.MIN_VALUE, a negative number, but the != 0 test still works because & keeps only that one bit either way.
hints: 1 << bit builds a number whose only 1 is at position `bit` (1 << 3 is 8, binary 1000).
value & mask keeps only that one bit of value and zeroes all the others.
Return (value & mask) != 0 -- comparing to 0 works even for bit 31, where the mask itself is negative.
